Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script) to finish the whole workflow.  
I’ve also included the exact file contents you’ll need to add to the repo.

> **⚠️**  
> *These instructions assume you have `git`, `docker`, `kubectl`, and `gh` (GitHub CLI) installed and authenticated on the machine you’re running them from.*

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL with  
> `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the artefacts

### 2.1 Inspect the repo

Run a quick scan to see what the app looks like:

```bash
# List top‑level files
ls -R
```

Typical output for a minimal Node.js app:

```
├── Dockerfile          # (doesn't exist yet)
├── README.md
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── src
│   └── index.js
└── .github
    └── workflows
```

> *If the repo already contains a Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifests, you can skip or overwrite them.*

### 2.2 Create / update the Dockerfile

Create a `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```bash
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# Use an official Node runtime as a parent image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files and install dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["npm", "start"]
EOF
```

> **Why node:18‑alpine?**  
> It’s lightweight, stable, and the latest LTS at the time of writing.  
> Adjust the tag if you need a different Node version.

### 2.3 Create Kubernetes YAML files

Create a `k8s` directory and add two files: `deployment.yaml` and `service.yaml`.

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
```

#### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
  labels:
    app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use another registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

#### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Tip:**  
> If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` and adjust the `port` mapping accordingly.

### 2.4 Create a GitHub Actions workflow

Create a workflow file that builds the Docker image, pushes it to GitHub Container Registry, and optionally deploys to a cluster.

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF'
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest

    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes (optional)
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      uses: azure/k8s-deploy@v4
      with:
        manifests: |
          k8s/deployment.yaml
          k8s/service.yaml
        images: |
          ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
        kubeconfig: ${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG }}
EOF
```

> **What this does**  
> * Builds the image from the Dockerfile.  
> * Pushes it to `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> * If you have a `KUBECONFIG` secret set up, it will apply the manifests to your cluster.  
> * Remove the “Deploy to Kubernetes” step if you don’t want automatic deployment.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml k8s/service.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run on the `main` branch, building the image and (optionally) deploying it.

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas of the app |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app inside the cluster |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image (and deploys) |

Feel free to tweak the Docker base image, Node version, replica count, or service type to match your production needs. Happy coding!
